definition: Determining the legal meaning of contractual terms by applying principles of English law to the text and relevant context.
example: A solicitor examines a disputed pricing clause and advises how a court may construe it.

definition: Determining the meaning and application of legal authorities in a particular factual and jurisdictional context.
example: A legal researcher compares the wording of a statute with decisions interpreting it.

definition: A clinical decision support product that supplies criteria for reviewing the appropriateness of services and levels of care.
example: A utilization reviewer consults applicable criteria when evaluating an inpatient stay.

definition: Administering a prescribed substance into the dermis in accordance with clinical requirements.
example: A qualified clinician administers a diagnostic skin test and records it.

definition: Monitoring nervous system function during surgery to help detect changes that may call for clinical action.
example: A monitoring specialist alerts the surgical team to a significant change in recorded signals.

definition: Small dental cameras used to capture images from inside a patient's mouth.
example: A dentist shows a patient an image of a damaged tooth captured during examination.

definition: Providing fluids intravenously to treat or prevent inadequate hydration under appropriate clinical direction.
example: A care team monitors a patient's response to ordered intravenous fluids.

definition: Delivering prescribed fluids, medications, or nutrients into a vein over time under applicable clinical procedures.
example: A nurse checks an authorized infusion order and monitors the patient during administration.

definition: Software for tracking stock quantities, locations, movements, and replenishment needs.
example: A warehouse checks available quantity before assigning stock to an order.

definition: Conducting authorized evidence-based inquiries into suspected unlawful distribution of controlled drugs.
example: An authorized investigator documents findings for a legally supervised case review.
sense_note: Non-operational scope; do not infer authority or permitted investigative techniques.

definition: Gathering relevant and reliable information through planned, impartial questioning and careful documentation.
example: An investigator uses open questions to obtain a witness's account before checking specific details.

definition: Preparing and maintaining a clinical trial document that summarizes relevant nonclinical and clinical information about an investigational product.
example: A clinical team updates the brochure after receiving new safety findings.
sense_note: The label denotes a document; this definition reflects brochure preparation as the corresponding skill.

definition: A historical digital product design and collaboration platform used to share prototypes and collect feedback.
example: A team previously shared a clickable prototype and collected review comments in InVision.
sense_note: Confirm the specific InVision product because capabilities and operating status differ across products.

definition: Receiving, checking, coding, approving, and recording invoices for settlement under applicable controls.
example: An accounts payable clerk matches an invoice against its purchase order and flags discrepancies.

definition: A historical JavaScript runtime fork of Node.js that later rejoined the Node.js project.
example: A maintainer recognizes an io.js deployment in archived application documentation.

definition: A workplace management software product for coordinating space, assets, and facilities-related work.
example: A facilities team tracks room use and manages service requests.
sense_note: The label may denote historical branding or a specific current product within a larger suite.

definition: A historical Angular-based version of the Ionic framework for building hybrid mobile applications using web technologies.
example: A team uses Ionic 2 components to build application screens for both Android and iOS.
sense_note: The entry is version-specific; do not assume current Ionic conventions.

definition: Apple's mobile operating system for the iPhone.
example: A developer tests how an iPhone application behaves with iOS accessibility settings.

definition: Planning, allocating, tracking, and governing IP addresses and address ranges across networks.
example: A network administrator records a subnet allocation to prevent conflicting assignments.

definition: An enhanced interactive Python shell and associated computing tools for exploratory programming and analysis.
example: A researcher inspects intermediate results and plots data in an interactive session.

definition: A historical graphical report designer for creating report templates used by JasperReports.
example: A report author lays out invoice fields and totals in iReport Designer.

definition: A message queue service that lets distributed applications exchange messages asynchronously.
example: A web service enqueues a background task for a separate worker to process.

definition: An implementation of Python for the .NET ecosystem that supports interoperability with .NET code.
example: A developer calls an existing .NET library from an IronPython script.

definition: Applying and managing water supplies for crops based on soil, plant, and operational requirements.
example: A farm manager adjusts irrigation scheduling after rainfall reduces crop water demand.

definition: Applying an appropriate fluid to flush a body site during authorized clinical care.
example: A clinician records irrigation performed as part of prescribed wound care.
sense_note: Confirm the intended anatomical site if a more specific sense is needed.

definition: An international standard for measurement management systems and requirements associated with measurement processes and equipment.
example: A manufacturer uses the standard when reviewing how calibration records support reliable measurements.

definition: A series of international standards for evaluating the biological safety of medical devices.
example: A manufacturer considers the applicable ISO 10993 parts when planning biological evaluation.
sense_note: Specific tests depend on device contact and intended use.

definition: A family of international standards and guidance for environmental management.
example: An organization uses an applicable family standard to guide its environmental management system.

definition: An international standard for applying risk management to medical devices throughout their lifecycle.
example: A device manufacturer documents hazards, risk controls, and their effectiveness.

definition: An international standard specifying quality and competence requirements for medical laboratories.
example: A laboratory uses the requirements to review personnel competence and result quality.

definition: International guidance for auditing management systems, including planning and auditor competence.
example: An audit lead uses the guidance to plan interviews and document audit evidence.

definition: A series of functional safety standards for electrical and electronic systems in production road vehicles.
example: An automotive engineering team traces a safety goal to system requirements and verification evidence.

definition: International guidance for integrating risk management principles and processes into organizational decisions.
example: A project team uses ISO 31000 guidance to structure a risk assessment and follow-up plan.

definition: An international standard specifying requirements for energy management systems and improvement of energy performance.
example: A manufacturing site tracks energy performance against its established baseline.

definition: An international standard for messages exchanged in card-originated financial transactions.
example: A payment system interprets the transaction message fields under an agreed ISO 8583 implementation.

definition: A core international standard describing quality management fundamentals and vocabulary, also commonly used to refer to the associated family of standards.
example: A team consults ISO 9000 vocabulary when interpreting a quality management requirement.
sense_note: ISO 9000 is not the certifiable system requirements standard ISO 9001.

definition: A family of international standards for information security management systems and related information security practices.
example: A security team consults relevant series guidance when preparing its management system.
sense_note: The series includes but is not identical to the requirements document ISO/IEC 27001.

definition: An international standard specifying requirements for establishing, maintaining, and improving an information security management system.
example: An organization assesses its security management system against the standard's requirements.

definition: A multipart international standard that defines SQL language features and their semantics for working with relational data.
example: A developer compares a query feature against the applicable ISO SQL specification before relying on portability.

definition: Software that records issues, assigns responsibility, and tracks their status from reporting through resolution.
example: A development team assigns a reported defect and records the verification that closes it.
